export const meta = {
  name: 'ci-speed-investigate',
  description: 'Measure and analyze treams-rs CI bottlenecks, then synthesize a ranked speed-up plan',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Investigate', detail: 'compile, pytest, wheels, topology, platform facts in parallel' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', detail: 'ranked proposals with projected critical path' },
  ],
}

const COMMON = `
You are part of an investigation into making the CI of the Rust+PyO3 project yaugenst/treams-rs faster WITHOUT sacrificing thoroughness
(no dropped coverage, no weaker checks; equivalent-or-better guarantees only — if an idea trades thoroughness, flag it explicitly as such).
READ FIRST: scratch: ci-speed/context.md (timings, facts, paths). Workflow files live in any of the worktrees under .github/workflows/.
HARD RULES:
- Never modify treams-rs (user's live checkout with uncommitted work). Read-only there is fine but prefer the worktrees.
- Do not push, open PRs, comment, re-run or dispatch workflows, or change any GitHub state. Read-only gh/gh api calls are fine.
- Report MEASURED numbers where you can, with the exact command used. Clearly separate measured facts from estimates/inference.
- Wall-clock matters only on the critical path: a saving in a job that is not on the critical path is worth ~0 unless it also shortens the second tier (~8.5 min jobs).
`

const INVEST = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    measurements: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      what: { type: 'string' }, value: { type: 'string' }, method: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['what', 'value', 'method'] } },
    findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      title: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' }, implication: { type: 'string' },
      confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] } }, required: ['title', 'evidence', 'implication', 'confidence'] } },
    proposals: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      change: { type: 'string' }, files: { type: 'string' }, est_saving: { type: 'string' },
      thoroughness_impact: { type: 'string' }, risk: { type: 'string' }, notes: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['change', 'est_saving', 'thoroughness_impact', 'risk'] } },
    open_questions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['measurements', 'findings', 'proposals'],
}

const TASKS = [
  { key: 'compile', prompt: `${COMMON}
YOUR FOCUS: Rust compile time and caching. Work ONLY in treams-ci-compile. Pin ALL builds to cores 0-3 (taskset -c 0-3, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4) to emulate a 4-vCPU runner.
1. Set up the env like CI's Python 3.12 lane (uv sync --locked --no-install-project --group dev --extra jax --extra autograd --python 3.12; torch CPU is not needed for building). Then time a CLEAN \`just build-ext\` (maturin develop, dev profile). Calibrate vs CI (236s).
2. Get a crate-level breakdown: \`cargo build --timings\` (or maturin develop with CARGO_PROFILE... / cargo rustc for treams-py) for the dev-profile extension build. Which crates dominate (faer? nalgebra? pyo3? treams-core itself)? How long does treams-core + treams-py alone take?
3. Simulate a warm-cache PR: after the clean build, touch/modify a file in crates/treams-core/src and in crates/treams-py/src and time the incremental rebuild with deps cached (this approximates Swatinem/rust-cache hit; note rust-cache does NOT cache workspace crates' incremental state, so also measure with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 which is what rust-cache sets).
4. Same for the Rust job: time \`cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings\` and \`cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features\` clean vs warm-deps; split compile vs test-execution time for cargo test (e.g. cargo test --no-run then run).
5. Measure target/ sizes (dev deps for extension, test build, release) to estimate GitHub Actions cache footprint vs the 10 GB repo cache limit across lanes (13 python lanes on 4 Python versions, 2 rust lanes, 20 wheel builds). Propose a concrete cache keying scheme (e.g. Swatinem/rust-cache shared-key per python-version/profile, save-if only on main) or sccache, and estimate hit-path timings from your measurements.
Note that each of the 13 Python lanes (Python 3.12-3.15, NumPy 2.1-2.5 on 3.12, frameworks lanes on 3.12/3.13/3.14) rebuilds the extension: pyo3 config differs per Python version, so think about which lanes can share a cache key.` },

  { key: 'pytest', prompt: `${COMMON}
YOUR FOCUS: Python test-suite runtime. Work ONLY in treams-ci-pytest. Pin timed runs to cores 4-7 (taskset -c 4-7) to emulate a 4-vCPU runner; builds may also use 4-7.
1. Reproduce the CI Python 3.12 lane env exactly (see ci.yml 'Install dependencies': uv sync --locked --no-install-project --group dev --extra jax --extra autograd --python 3.12, then CPU torch from the PyTorch CPU index at the locked version), then \`just build-ext\`.
2. Time the full suite: HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=ci taskset -c 4-7 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --durations=60 -q. Calibrate vs CI (~234s for non-coverage lanes, 303s with --cov). Also time with --cov=treams_rs to measure coverage overhead.
3. Characterize where time goes: top slow tests/files, hypothesis-heavy tests, oracle (pure-python treams) comparisons, framework import cost (jax/torch import time), collection time (pytest --collect-only timing).
4. Try pytest-xdist: install it into the scratch venv only (uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python pytest-xdist). Run with -n 4 (and -n auto / --dist loadfile / loadgroup variants) under taskset -c 4-7, with and without TREAMS_RS_NUM_THREADS=1. Does the suite pass identically (same pass/skip/xfail counts)? Which tests break or are order/process sensitive (thread pool tests, memory error tests, float environment tests, global state)? Does coverage still combine correctly with xdist (pytest-cov supports it)? Report speedup.
5. Check whether test time is dominated by native code compiled at dev opt-level: build with \`just build-ext-release\` (maturin develop --release) and re-time the suite. Note the dev profile intentionally keeps debug assertions — losing them would reduce thoroughness, so report it as data, not necessarily a proposal.
6. Inspect tests/conftest.py and tests/test_suite_rules.py for anything that assumes a single process (collection policy, stash, unavailable-requirement reporting) that would need adapting for xdist.` },

  { key: 'wheels', prompt: `${COMMON}
YOUR FOCUS: the Native Wheels matrix (.github/workflows/native-wheels.yml; reused by release-candidate.yml so the release path must stay at least as strong). Work in treams-ci-wheels; pin any local builds to cores 8-11.
Investigate and quantify:
1. abi3 feasibility: could treams-py use pyo3 abi3-py312 so one wheel per platform covers 3.12-3.15? grep crates/treams-py/src for pyo3::ffi / numpy C-API / ufunc creation / buffer protocol / anything outside the limited API; check pyo3 0.29 and rust-numpy 0.29 abi3 support (cargo source in installed tools: src). Performance or functionality implications. Note: this changes released artifacts, so it is a product decision — report feasibility and tradeoffs, not a recommendation to silently switch.
2. Multi-interpreter builds per platform job (maturin -i python3.12 python3.13 ... in one invocation) to reduce job count (macOS queueing: 8 macOS jobs vs ~5 concurrent macOS slots). Measure locally: release build of treams-py for one interpreter from clean, then for a second interpreter in the same target dir — how much recompiles (pyo3 config differs per interpreter)? Use \`taskset -c 8-11 uv run --no-sync maturin build --release --locked -m crates/treams-py/Cargo.toml -i python3.12\` then -i python3.13 (install interpreters with uv python install if needed). Report clean vs second-interpreter times.
3. macOS Intel: macos-15-intel builds take 580-706s vs ~255-330s on macos-latest arm64. Options: cross-compile x86_64-apple-darwin on arm64 runner (maturin-action target x86_64 on macos-latest), smoke-testing under Rosetta 2 (is it available on GitHub's arm64 macOS images?), universal2. Weigh: does cross-compiling + Rosetta smoke test preserve the guarantee that the shipped x86_64 wheel is tested on x86_64? Keep at least one native Intel smoke test?
4. maturin-action caching: it has an \`sccache: true\` input — how does it work for manylinux docker builds and macOS/Windows? Any caveats (release LTO builds and sccache hit rates, CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS with remapped paths per job breaking cache keys?). Also check scripts/wheel_build_paths.py — rustflags embed --remap-path-prefix with paths; are they identical across jobs of the same platform?
5. Per-job overheads visible in scratch: ci-speed/jobs-*.jsonl (e.g. setup-python 3.15 prerelease taking ~95s on macOS Intel, smoke-test 20-60s, Windows build ~400s).
Produce proposals with estimated per-job and critical-path savings, and say for each whether the release path (release-candidate.yml) is affected.` },

  { key: 'topology', prompt: `${COMMON}
YOUR FOCUS: CI job graph, critical path, redundancy and serialization. Mostly read-only analysis (worktree treams-ci-compile for reading files is fine; do not build there — another agent is timing builds in it).
1. Build an accurate critical-path model from scratch: ci-speed/jobs-*.jsonl (4 runs): per job start/end relative to run start, queue time, and the top-3 paths that bound wall-clock. Include the 'CI Success' and 'Coverage' tail jobs.
2. Python 3.12 lane does everything serially (actionlint, release guard self-test, \`just check\` incl. pre-commit file hygiene + docs-check, pytest --cov, \`just check-wheel\`). Propose a split into parallel jobs and compute the new critical path. Check exactly what \`just check\` and \`just check-wheel\` do (justfile, .pre-commit-config.yaml) and whether each piece needs the built extension.
3. Redundancy audit: is \`just check-wheel\` (host release build + build-path check + smoke base/advect/autograd/io) fully covered by Native Wheels / Linux x86-64 / Python 3.12 (manylinux build + build-path check + same smoke profiles + dependency-minimum smoke)? What, if anything, would be lost by moving/dropping it (e.g. validates the developer \`just check-wheel\` recipe or a non-manylinux host build)? Other duplicated work: docs.yml rebuilding the extension, Rust lanes both running full cargo test, sdist building a wheel, numpy lanes, etc. Distinguish duplication that adds coverage from duplication that does not.
4. Look at the failed/cancelled runs (37120335440, 37118883232, 37117567002 failure; 37123347405 cancelled) via \`gh run view <id> --json jobs\` and logs as needed (gh run view --log-failed, keep output small): which lanes caught real failures? This tells which lanes carry unique thoroughness value.
5. Concurrency: native-wheels.yml has a workflow-level concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: false while ci.yml cancels in progress. When called via workflow_call from CI, does the inner group block a newer push's wheel jobs until the old ones finish? Check GitHub semantics and the run history for evidence.
6. Trigger hygiene: are there doc-only/paths-ignore opportunities that would not weaken required checks (ci-success must still report)? Consider but be skeptical.
Output proposals with critical-path deltas.` },

  { key: 'platform', prompt: `${COMMON}
YOUR FOCUS: GitHub Actions platform facts that the speed-up options depend on. Use web research (load WebSearch/WebFetch via ToolSearch) and cite URLs + dates; prefer docs.github.com and official project docs/changelogs. Today is 2026-10-03.
Answer, with sources:
1. Concurrency limits for a PUBLIC repo on a personal account: total concurrent jobs and concurrent macOS jobs for GitHub-hosted standard runners. Observed: 8 macOS jobs, 3 queued 6-9 min.
2. Standard runner specs for public repos: ubuntu-latest/24.04 (vCPU/RAM), ubuntu-24.04-arm, macos-latest (arm64 M-series, vCPU), macos-15-intel, windows-latest. Any free larger runners for public repos?
3. macOS Intel runner future: macos-15-intel deprecation/retirement timeline; GitHub statements about x86_64 macOS support. Is Rosetta 2 installed on GitHub's arm64 macOS images (macos-14/15/26)?
4. Actions cache: per-repo size limit (and whether it can be raised now), eviction policy, branch scoping (can a pull_request run restore caches saved on main? can it restore caches from its own PR ref across pushes? can main restore PR caches?), cache upload/download throughput in practice.
5. Swatinem/rust-cache current version: what it caches (registry, git, target deps only; workspace crates excluded?), CARGO_INCREMENTAL handling, shared-key/key/save-if/cache-workspace-crates options, typical behavior with multiple jobs.
6. sccache with the GHA cache backend (SCCACHE_GHA_ENABLED): reliability, rate limiting, does it cache when CARGO_INCREMENTAL is on, works in maturin-action manylinux containers (maturin-action sccache input), interaction with LTO / -C remap-path-prefix rustflags (cache key includes rustflags and absolute paths?).
7. pytest-xdist + pytest-cov combination support (current versions) and Hypothesis with xdist (database, derandomize).
8. maturin: building multiple interpreters in one \`maturin build -i ...\` invocation — does it reuse the compiled dependency graph between interpreters? abi3 + rust-numpy (numpy crate) support status.
Return each as a finding with evidence = quoted/cited source and URL.` },
]

phase('Investigate')
const results = await parallel(TASKS.map(t => () =>
  agent(t.prompt, { label: `investigate:${t.key}`, phase: 'Investigate', schema: INVEST })
    .then(r => r ? { key: t.key, ...r } : null)))
const ok = results.filter(Boolean)
log(`Investigators returned: ${ok.map(r => r.key).join(', ')}`)

phase('Synthesize')
const SYN = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    current_critical_path: { type: 'string' },
    proposals: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string' }, title: { type: 'string' }, change_detail: { type: 'string' }, files: { type: 'string' },
      wall_clock_effect: { type: 'string' }, thoroughness: { type: 'string', enum: ['improves', 'unchanged', 'reduces', 'tradeoff'] },
      thoroughness_notes: { type: 'string' }, risk: { type: 'string' }, complexity: { type: 'string', enum: ['S', 'M', 'L'] },
      affects_release_path: { type: 'boolean' }, depends_on: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['id', 'title', 'change_detail', 'wall_clock_effect', 'thoroughness', 'risk', 'complexity', 'affects_release_path', 'evidence'] } },
    projected_critical_path: { type: 'string' },
    rejected_ideas: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { idea: { type: 'string' }, reason: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['idea', 'reason'] } },
    unknowns: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['current_critical_path', 'proposals', 'projected_critical_path', 'rejected_ideas'],
}
const synthesis = await agent(`${COMMON}
You are the synthesizer. Below are the structured results of five parallel investigations (compile/caching, pytest runtime, native wheels, job topology, GitHub platform facts).
Produce a ranked, de-duplicated set of concrete CI changes for treams-rs. For each: exact change (which job/step/file, config snippet sketch if useful),
wall-clock effect ON THE CRITICAL PATH (not per-job), thoroughness verdict (improves/unchanged/reduces/tradeoff) with justification,
risk (cache poisoning/staleness, flakiness, release-path effects, maintenance), complexity, dependencies between changes, and evidence pointers to measurements.
Then project the new critical path if the 'unchanged/improves' set is applied together (state assumptions, e.g. cache hit rate on PRs, first-run cold cache).
Prefer few high-leverage changes over many micro-optimizations; list micro-optimizations and rejected ideas separately with reasons.
Resolve contradictions between investigators explicitly (say which evidence wins and why). You may read repo files in treams-ci-compile to confirm details; do not run builds.

INVESTIGATION RESULTS:
${JSON.stringify(ok, null, 1)}`, { label: 'synthesize', phase: 'Synthesize', schema: SYN })

return { investigations: ok, synthesis }
export const meta = {
  name: 'ci-speed-implement-verify',
  description: 'Implement the thoroughness-preserving CI speed-ups on a local branch, adversarially verify, then fix',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Implement', detail: 'commit-per-change on ci/speed-up (local only)' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'thoroughness, correctness, speed lenses + completeness critic' },
    { title: 'Fix', detail: 'apply confirmed issues, re-validate' },
  ],
}

const BASE = `
Project: yaugenst/treams-rs (Rust + PyO3 extension, Python package). Goal: faster CI WITHOUT sacrificing thoroughness.
Prior investigation (measured data, proposals, rejected ideas): scratch: ci-speed/wf1.json (keys: investigations[], synthesis) and scratch: ci-speed/context.md.
Implementation branch: ci/speed-up checked out in treams-ci-speed (based on origin/main 5947c78). PR #1 has merged and v0.1.0 has been released, so main is the base.
HARD RULES: never modify treams-rs (user's checkout). Never push, open PRs, dispatch/re-run workflows, or change GitHub state (read-only gh api is fine).
No AI/model identifiers in commits or files. Prefer the smallest coherent change; reuse repo patterns; do not add speculative guards.
To emulate a 4-vCPU GitHub runner locally use taskset -c on 4 cores. The system uv (0.12.3) is too old for this repo; use scratch: ci-speed/uvbin-venv/bin/uv (0.12.22) by putting scratch: ci-speed/uvbin-venv/bin first on PATH. shellcheck/actionlint are not installed system-wide; fetch actionlint ${'1.7.12'} the same way ci.yml does (sha256-verified) into scratch: ci-speed/tools and get shellcheck via e.g. \`uvx --from shellcheck-py shellcheck\` or a pinned release binary in scratch: ci-speed/tools.
`

const IMPL_PROMPT = `${BASE}
You are the IMPLEMENTER. Work in treams-ci-speed on branch ci/speed-up. Read the synthesis proposals in scratch: ci-speed/wf1.json first (P1-P5, M1-M5) and the existing workflows, justfile, docs/development/*.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and the tests that parse workflows (grep tests/ and scripts/ for 'ci.yml', 'native-wheels', 'workflows').
Make ONE COMMIT PER CHANGE, in this order, with conventional-commit subjects matching the repo style (e.g. 'ci: ...', 'test: ...'):
 1. P2 — split the Python 3.12 lane: justfile gains \`check-static\` (everything in \`check\` except docs-check) and \`check: check-static docs-check\`; ci.yml 3.12 leg keeps build-ext + \`just docs-check\` + pytest --cov + coverage upload; new parallel job 'Repository checks' (same env incl. torch CPU since pyrefly needs it; actionlint; release-guard self-test; \`just check-static\`); new parallel job 'Host release wheel' (minimal env per synthesis, TREAMS_RS_NUM_THREADS: "1" to match today's 3.12 lane where that env was set; \`just check-wheel\`). Verify which env vars the old 3.12 leg had (TREAMS_RS_NUM_THREADS=1 applied to EVERYTHING in that leg, including just check and pytest) and preserve equivalent semantics for each moved step. Wire both into ci-success needs + result loop. Update any docs/tests describing the CI layout.
 2. M1 — top-level ci.yml env CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: "0" with a short comment (debug assertions/overflow checks unaffected). Do NOT add CARGO_INCREMENTAL.
 3. P1 — native-wheels.yml: on macOS legs and only when inputs.source_revision == '' (i.e. never for release-candidate builds), install the pinned toolchain via dtolnay/rust-toolchain (same pinned sha as elsewhere, toolchain 1.94.0) and add Swatinem/rust-cache pinned by full commit sha (look up the v2.9.2 or current latest release sha with read-only gh api; add the version comment like other pins), placed AFTER 'Remap local build paths' and BEFORE 'Build portable wheel'; shared-key per platform artifact; save only from the 3.12 leg (decide whether to also save on PR runs — PR caches are PR-scoped and let later pushes of the same PR hit when main's cache is cold or evicted after 7 idle days; justify your choice in the commit body). Check the repo's action allow-list/pinning policy (tests or docs may enforce sha pins and an allow-list of actions — grep for 'allow' and 'uses:' checks in tests/scripts) and update it if needed.
 4. P4 — pytest-xdist: adapt scratch: ci-speed/pytest-agent/proposal.patch (built against an older commit) to main: dev dependency pytest-xdist>=3.8,<4 with a minimal uv.lock update (uv lock, verify only pytest-xdist+execnet added), conftest workeroutput/pytest_testnodedown merge so the Rayon global-pool guard and the unavailable-dependency report still work under xdist, explicit \`-n auto\` on the 4 CI pytest invocations (NOT PYTEST_ADDOPTS/ini), COVERAGE_CORE: sysmon on the 3.12 coverage step, plus M4: a regression test proving the Rayon global-pool guard fails the session both serially and with -n 2 (look at how test_collection_policy runs nested pytest). Update docs/development/testing.md if it documents how to run tests.
 5. P3 (DRAFT, separate final commit so it can be dropped): cross-compile macOS x86-64 wheels on macos-latest and smoke-test each on macos-15-intel in a new job that downloads the artifact; keep artifact names and the wheelhouse matrix shape so release tooling/tests keep working; avoid duplicating the smoke loop (move it to a script if needed); ensure release-candidate's downstream jobs still depend on the Intel smoke (they need the whole called workflow). Mark the commit body: 'Untested on GitHub runners; needs one CI trial before relying on it.'
VALIDATE after each commit where relevant, and at the end: actionlint with shellcheck on all workflows; set up the CI env (uv sync --locked --no-install-project --group dev --extra jax --extra autograd --python 3.12 + CPU torch at the locked version like ci.yml) and run \`just check-static\`, \`just docs-check\`, the workflow/release tests, then the FULL suite twice under taskset -c 0-3 with HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=ci CI=true: serially and with -n auto; compare pass/skip/xfail counts. Also \`uv lock --check\`. Use CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 for builds to save time.
Do not push. Leave the worktree clean (all work committed). Return a precise report.`

const IMPL_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    commits: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      sha: { type: 'string' }, subject: { type: 'string' }, summary: { type: 'string' }, diffstat: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['sha', 'subject', 'summary'] } },
    validation: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      check: { type: 'string' }, command: { type: 'string' }, result: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['check', 'result'] } },
    deviations: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    open_issues: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['commits', 'validation', 'deviations', 'open_issues'],
}

const VERDICT = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    per_change: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      change: { type: 'string' }, verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['confirmed', 'needs_fix', 'refuted'] }, rationale: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['change', 'verdict', 'rationale'] } },
    issues: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocker', 'major', 'minor', 'nit'] }, change: { type: 'string' },
      description: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' }, suggested_fix: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['severity', 'change', 'description', 'evidence', 'suggested_fix'] } },
    summary: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['per_change', 'issues', 'summary'],
}

phase('Implement')
const impl = await agent(IMPL_PROMPT, { label: 'implement', phase: 'Implement', schema: IMPL_SCHEMA })
if (!impl) return { error: 'implementer failed' }
log(`Implemented ${impl.commits.length} commits`)

const VCOMMON = `${BASE}
You are an ADVERSARIAL VERIFIER. The implementer committed changes on ci/speed-up (see \`git -C treams-ci-speed log --stat origin/main..ci/speed-up\` and the per-commit diffs). Implementer report:
${JSON.stringify(impl, null, 1)}
Do NOT edit treams-ci-speed. If you need to run anything that writes files, make your own detached worktree under scratch: ci-speed/verify-<yourlens> from ci/speed-up and remove it (git worktree remove --force) when done. Default to skepticism: a claim is not confirmed until you have checked it against the code, GitHub semantics docs, or measurement. Report concrete issues with evidence and a suggested fix; do not pad with style nits.`

const LENSES = [
  { key: 'thoroughness', prompt: `${VCOMMON}
LENS: THOROUGHNESS. Prove or refute that NO check got weaker. Build a before/after inventory of every command, env var and matrix leg that executes in CI (ci.yml, native-wheels.yml, docs.yml, release-candidate.yml) per job, and diff it: every check that ran before must still run with equivalent inputs (e.g. TREAMS_RS_NUM_THREADS=1 previously applied to the whole 3.12 leg: just check, docs-check, pytest --cov and check-wheel — does each still run with the same thread setting? does the coverage lane still exercise the one-thread path?). Confirm ci-success blocks on every new job and cannot pass when a new job fails/skips. For xdist: confirm nothing is silently skipped (Rayon guard, unavailable-dependency report, nested pytest tests, tests that check process-global state, filterwarnings=error behaviour in workers, Hypothesis settings in workers). For the debug=0 change: confirm debug-assertions/overflow-checks unaffected and no test depends on debuginfo. For P1/P3: confirm release builds are unchanged or equally strong and every shipped wheel is still smoke-tested on its real target hardware.` },
  { key: 'correctness', prompt: `${VCOMMON}
LENS: CORRECTNESS & RISK of the workflow/YAML/test changes. Check: GitHub expression semantics (inputs.* in workflow_call vs workflow_dispatch vs absent; github.ref inside reusable workflows; runner.os; save-if; matrix include/exclude), job/step ordering (rust-cache needs the toolchain and the remap rustflags env before it computes its key; maturin-action reinstalling toolchains), cache scoping/poisoning (PR scope vs main, fork PRs), actionlint+shellcheck cleanliness (run them), repository tests that parse workflows (run the relevant ones), the action pin/allow-list policy, conftest hook correctness under xdist (pytest_testnodedown signature, optionalhook, workeroutput serialisability via execnet — sets/defaultdicts/tuples?), uv.lock minimality, justfile recipe semantics (does \`just check\` locally still do exactly what it did?). For the P3 draft: wheel tag/MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET when cross-compiling with maturin-action on macos-latest, setup-python arch on the build runner (the interpreter used for -i python must be valid for an x86_64 target when cross compiling — check how maturin handles --interpreter python on a cross build and whether pyo3 needs PYO3_CROSS_* settings), artifact names, release-candidate needs graph.` },
  { key: 'speed', prompt: `${VCOMMON}
LENS: SPEED CLAIMS. Independently re-derive the current critical path from GitHub job data (use scratch: ci-speed/jobs-*.jsonl and also fetch the post-merge main push run's jobs: \`gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main --limit 3\` then \`gh api repos/yaugenst/treams-rs/actions/runs/<id>/jobs?per_page=100\`). Then, for the implemented branch, estimate the new critical path per change and combined, separating warm-cache vs cold-cache runs and first-PR-push vs later pushes. Challenge the synthesis numbers: the macOS dependency-phase share (check real macOS 'Build portable wheel' logs via \`gh api repos/yaugenst/treams-rs/actions/jobs/<job_id>/logs\` — keep output small, grep for Compiling treams-core / Finished timestamps), rust-cache restore/save overhead on macOS, whether P2's new jobs push peak concurrency over the account's limit, whether xdist actually helps on 4-vCPU runners given rayon threading. State plainly which changes move wall-clock and which only save runner minutes or improve time-to-first-failure.` },
  { key: 'critic', prompt: `${VCOMMON}
LENS: COMPLETENESS CRITIC. What is missing? Consider levers the investigation did not evaluate or dismissed too quickly, e.g.: faer/nalgebra feature trimming or dependency-level profile overrides that speed compile without changing semantics; whether the release profile's codegen-units=1 could be relaxed only for PR wheel builds and what that would cost in thoroughness; abi3 (P5) more concretely (what would the matrix look like, how big is the perf cost really); cancelling superseded runs; merge queue; running the native wheel matrix only on main/merge queue (thoroughness tradeoff — quantify); GitHub support raising the macOS cap; Windows becoming the next bound; flaky-test risk under xdist; the cold-cache problem for a low-traffic repo (7-day eviction) and whether a cheap scheduled cache warm-up is justified. Also check for claims in scratch: ci-speed/wf1.json that look unverified (e.g. the 'cache-mode: none' GitHub feature said to be from 2026-09-10 — verify via web sources; load WebSearch/WebFetch with ToolSearch). Rank what is worth adding vs not, honestly.` },
]

phase('Verify')
const verdicts = await parallel(LENSES.map(l => () =>
  agent(l.prompt, { label: `verify:${l.key}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT }).then(v => v ? { lens: l.key, ...v } : null)))
const vs = verdicts.filter(Boolean)
const actionable = vs.flatMap(v => v.issues.filter(i => i.severity === 'blocker' || i.severity === 'major' || i.severity === 'minor').map(i => ({ lens: v.lens, ...i })))
log(`Verifiers: ${vs.length}; actionable issues: ${actionable.length}`)

phase('Fix')
let fix = null
if (actionable.length) {
  fix = await agent(`${BASE}
You are the FIXER. Verifiers reviewed the commits on ci/speed-up in treams-ci-speed. Their issues (blocker/major/minor) are below, plus the full verdicts.
For each issue: decide if it is valid (re-check the evidence yourself; verifiers can be wrong). Fix valid ones with the smallest change, amending into the commit the issue belongs to (use \`git commit --fixup <sha>\` then \`git rebase --autosquash\` non-interactively via GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=true git rebase -i --autosquash origin/main) so the one-commit-per-change structure is kept. Skip invalid ones with a reason. Skip 'add a new lever' suggestions from the critic unless trivially small and clearly within the thoroughness-preserving set — just list them.
Re-run validation affected by your fixes (actionlint+shellcheck, workflow tests, and the full suite with -n auto under taskset -c 0-3 if tests/conftest changed). Do not push. Leave the worktree clean.
ISSUES:
${JSON.stringify(actionable, null, 1)}
FULL VERDICTS:
${JSON.stringify(vs, null, 1)}`, { label: 'fix', phase: 'Fix', schema: {
    type: 'object',
    properties: {
      handled: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
        issue: { type: 'string' }, action: { type: 'string', enum: ['fixed', 'skipped_invalid', 'skipped_out_of_scope'] }, detail: { type: 'string' } },
        required: ['issue', 'action', 'detail'] } },
      final_commits: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
      validation: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    },
    required: ['handled', 'final_commits', 'validation'] } })
}
return { impl, verdicts: vs, fix }
